code-fact.description: something structurally true about a config or a script — what a module owns, what a function guarantees
code-fact.read_when: labelling a claim about how the code is built

decision.description: what was chosen and what it beat — dated

documentation.description: how to use or operate — references, indexes, the protocol; must match reality, and may carry its own headings
documentation.read_when: writing a reference or an index

fact.description: something true about the world that is not about this repo — the catch-all
fact.read_when: labelling a claim that no more specific word fits

grammar.description: one custom name — what the word names here, where it first appeared, and the names it sits next to
grammar.read_when: meeting a word this repo uses in its own way, naming something new, or asking what a name already means

insight.description: a connection seen across memos — the non-obvious why, argued in the body; a bare claim is worth nothing

knowledge.description: what the repo is — how a config works, what a contract is; true until the config changes, fixed in the same change
knowledge.read_when: writing or trusting a knowledge memo

persona.description: one worn preprompt — who is working, in the second person, with the practitioners each behaviour is taken from
persona.read_when: writing a persona memo, wearing one, consulting one, or dispatching work to one

preference.description: what the person wants, standing across sessions — a tool, a style, a default
preference.read_when: labelling something the person wants held past this conversation

procedural.description: how we do X — a learned workflow, rule or convention, one sentence long
procedural.read_when: labelling a step or a rule rather than a fact

project.description: ongoing state of a thing being built — what runs, what is half-done, what it is blocked on
project.read_when: labelling where a piece of work stands

question.description: what is asked and not yet settled — one topic per file, `Q:` / `A: ?` blocks

reference.description: a pointer out of the record — a link, a document, a name to look up
reference.read_when: labelling an external address worth keeping

research.description: what was looked into — findings, open questions, what is not known yet; tentative, dated, names what would change it
research.read_when: writing or trusting a research memo

routine.description: a procedure — steps that plug memos together into one run, `name:` the invocation handle; followed literally or not at all

type.description: the one kind the gate hardcodes — a kind declaration, the only shape the index reads by name
type.read_when: adding a kind, or asking why the folders are what they are

work-memo.description: one unit of planned work — `level: 1-10`, `status: open | done | blocked`, a `## Do` and a `## Check`; done when the Check passes
